coverage: Weekend edition, week of Nov 9 to 13
moodReason: Hot October CPI pushed rate-hike bets higher while AI and chip stocks kept falling after the Nasdaq slipped into correction territory. Investors are still waiting on Nvidia's results on Nov 17.

stories.headline: Hot October CPI lifts odds of a December Fed rate hike
stories.what: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast, and core CPI rose 0.3% against 0.2% expected. The 2-year Treasury yield jumped to 4.69% and S&P 500 futures fell 0.6% on the morning of the release.
stories.why: Before the report, markets already priced a better than 80 percent chance of a quarter-point hike at the Dec 8 to 9 meeting. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a core reading around 0.3 percent or higher could justify considering a 50 basis point hike, so higher yields hit valuations.

stories.headline: Nvidia shares fall 6.5% as AI selloff deepens
stories.what: Nvidia fell 6.5% on Tuesday Nov 10 and was on track to lose more than $470 billion in market value over two sessions. Nasdaq Composite was down about 1% that afternoon. Nvidia also hired outside lawyers for an internal investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang.
stories.why: Nvidia is the largest AI bellwether, so its slide pulls the rest of the AI chain lower. The hot CPI print and the investigation headlines came on the same day, which made the drop worse.

stories.headline: Tech in correction after worst chip rout since 2020
stories.what: On Thursday Nov 5 the S&P 500 tech sector fell 7.3% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor index fell more than 12%, both their biggest one-day drops in more than six years. The Nasdaq Composite closed nearly 12% below its Oct 6 all-time high, past the 10% mark that defines a correction.
stories.why: Investors worry that Democratic midterm wins could slow the AI data center buildout. Truist strategist Keith Lerner called it a buyers' strike in tech, with tech lagging the S&P 500 by its widest margin since May 2002.

stories.headline: Data center equipment and neocloud stocks slide
stories.what: GE Vernova fell more than 6% after SoftBank revised its equipment procurement plans for US data center projects. Iren fell 10%, Nebius 7% and CoreWeave 3% on the same day. All three neocloud names are down at least 40% from the Nasdaq's Oct 6 high.
stories.why: Cuts to data center spending plans reduce demand for power equipment and cloud capacity, and they test how the AI buildout will be financed.

stories.headline: Anthropic IPO could price before Thanksgiving, timing not confirmed
stories.what: Reports say Anthropic is targeting a Nasdaq listing in mid to late November, possibly as early as the week of Nov 16, and that it publicly filed its S-1 on Oct 26. The company has not announced a date, and sources disagree on the timing.
stories.why: A very large AI listing could either refresh interest in the sector or draw money away from existing AI names, so the timing matters for the tech tape next week.

watch.item: Nvidia Q3 fiscal 2027 results and call at 2 p.m. PT
Possible Anthropic Nasdaq debut (date not confirmed)
FOMC meeting, with markets pricing a hike above 80 percent odds

bottomLine: Last week's inflation data reversed the earlier hope for a pause, and markets now price a likely December rate hike. Tech is in a correction led by Nvidia and the AI infrastructure names, and the sell-off has spread to power and data center stocks. The next test is Nvidia's results on Nov 17, which will show whether the AI buildout can keep its momentum. Index closes for Nov 9 to 13 could not be verified from the sources available, so the snapshot uses the latest verified levels and is dated.
